title: omxcore: a file, a planner, CPU or GPU kernels
subtitle: SQL over the files you already have; the planner picks the device, and says why

nodes.label: mx
nodes.desc: One native program, no Python: mx sql "SELECT …" prints rows, the time, the device and notes as JSON.

nodes.label: Python
nodes.desc: Lazy frames: nothing runs until compute(). Published as mxframe.

nodes.label: Your app
nodes.desc: Apps link the engine like SQLite. omxplorer runs every query through it, in the same process.

nodes.label: Parser
nodes.desc: Joins, CTEs, subqueries, windows, QUALIFY. A typo comes back with a line, a column and 'did you mean'.

nodes.label: Planner
nodes.desc: Prices the CPU and the GPU for this query on this machine, copies included, and picks one. The answer names where it ran.
nodes.notes: Informal: 2.7× GPU over CPU on a 2-core budget; with 12 cores AUTO keeps the CPU.

nodes.label: CPU kernels
nodes.desc: Parallel Mojo kernels. All 22 TPC-H queries at SF10 in 3.15 s (DuckDB 5.08 s).

nodes.label: GPU kernels
nodes.desc: The same queries as GPU kernels, written in Mojo too. NVIDIA on Linux; Apple's Metal on GitHub's macOS runners.

nodes.label: Your files
nodes.desc: No import, no new format. Files bigger than memory stream a row group at a time: a 1.6 GB file in 72 MB.

steps.note: mx sql: revenue by return flag, from lineitem.parquet.
Parsed and checked; a typo would come back with 'did you mean'.
AUTO prices both devices, copies included, and picks the cheaper one.
Here the CPU wins, so it runs there.
Only the columns it needs are read: 3 of 16.
JSON back: rows, exact decimals, the time and the device it ran on.
omxplorer asks for a group-by from Mojo, no SQL text needed.
On a big table the GPU is cheaper, so the kernels run there.
The file streams in; nothing is copied into a new format.
The totals land in the sheet, in the same process: no server, no JSON.
